title: The 10 Best Cordless Finish Nailers
subtitle: Battery-powered 15- and 16-gauge finish nailers for trim with no compressor or hose, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A cordless finish nailer drives 15 or 16-gauge trim nails with no compressor, hose or gas cartridge, which makes punch-list and single-room trim jobs far quicker to set up. We ranked 10 best-sellers on rating, review volume and features (a brushless motor, switchable sequential and bump fire, a battery in the box and a 3-year-plus warranty). Expect 6 to 9 lbs, heavier than an air nailer. They run from about $149 for CRAFTSMAN's bare CMCN616B to $412 for the DEWALT DCN660D1 kit.

products.name: DEWALT 20V MAX Finish Nailer, Angled, 16GA, Tool Only (DCN660B)
products.verdict: The most-reviewed cordless finish nailer here: a brushless 16-gauge angled nailer with a tool-free sequential/contact switch, depth adjustment and jam release.
products.skip_if: You don't own DEWALT batteries; the DCN660D1 kit adds one.
pros: Tool-free mode, depth and jam release

products.name: DEWALT 20V MAX XR Finish Nailer, Angled, 16GA, Kit (DCN660D1)
products.verdict: The DCN660 as a kit with a 2.0Ah battery, charger and box: the highest-rated cordless finish nailer here.
products.best_for: Starting on DEWALT 20V with a finish nailer.
products.skip_if: You already own DEWALT batteries; the bare DCN660B is $24 less.

products.name: DEWALT 20V MAX XR Cordless 15-Gauge Angled Finish Nailer, Tool Only (DCN650B)
products.verdict: DEWALT's 15-gauge for crown, casing and hardwood flooring, with a micro nose for seeing where the nail goes.
products.best_for: Heavy trim and door casing on DEWALT 20V.
products.skip_if: You mostly do baseboard; 16-gauge leaves smaller holes.

products.name: DEWALT 20V MAX XR Finish Nailer, Straight, 16GA, Tool Only (DCN662B)
products.verdict: The straight-magazine version of DEWALT's 16-gauge, which takes cheaper straight finish nails, with a micro nose and a brushless motor.
products.best_for: DEWALT owners who'd rather buy straight 16-gauge nails.
products.skip_if: You need to reach into tight corners; the angled DCN660 fits better.
cons: Straight magazine is less nimble in corners

products.name: Metabo HPT 18V MultiVolt Brushless Cordless 16 Gauge Straight Finish Nailer Kit (NT1865DMST)
products.verdict: An air-spring drive that fires with no ramp-up, like a pneumatic, plus a selective actuation switch, battery, charger and bag, and Metabo HPT's lifetime tool-body warranty.
products.best_for: Trim pros who want air-nailer feel and a lifetime warranty.
products.skip_if: You want a long track record; it has 89 reviews.

products.name: Metabo HPT 18V Brushless 15 Gauge Angled Finish Nailer, Kit (NT1865DAA)
products.verdict: Metabo HPT's new 15-gauge kit: 13% lighter and smaller than its predecessor, rated for flush drives into hardwood and fiber cement, up to 700 nails per charge, and a lifetime tool-body warranty.
products.best_for: Heavy trim in hardwood and fiber cement.
products.skip_if: Price matters; at $399 it's the second most expensive here.

products.name: Milwaukee 3020-20 M18 FUEL Gen II 16-Gauge Straight Finish Nailer (Tool Only)
products.verdict: Milwaukee's second-generation M18 FUEL 16-gauge fires three nails a second with sequential and contact modes, tool-free depth and jam clearing, and an LED.
products.best_for: M18 owners doing full trim packages.
products.skip_if: You want a battery in the box; this is the bare tool.

products.name: CRAFTSMAN V20 Cordless Finish Nailer, 16 Gauge, Bare Tool Only (CMCN616B)
products.verdict: A V20 16-gauge for about $150 less than DEWALT's, with tool-free jam and stall settings and a 3-year warranty, rated for up to 375 nails per charge.
products.best_for: CRAFTSMAN V20 owners trimming a room or two.
products.skip_if: You trim every day; DEWALT and Metabo are brushless.

products.name: CRAFTSMAN V20 Cordless Finish Nailer Kit, 16GA, Battery and Charger Included (CMCN616C1)
products.verdict: The CMCN616 as a kit with battery and charger, rated a little higher than the bare tool listing.
products.skip_if: You own V20 batteries; the bare tool saves about $113.
cons: Costs nearly as much as DEWALT's bare tool

products.name: Makita XNB02Z 18V LXT Straight Finish Nailer, 16 Gauge, 2-1/2"
products.verdict: Makita's LXT 16-gauge straight nailer drives 1 to 2-1/2 inch nails, up to 1,000 per 5.0Ah charge, with dry-fire lockout and a compact nose for tight spots.
products.best_for: Makita 18V owners who want a finish nailer on batteries they already have.
products.skip_if: You want a brushless motor; this listing doesn't claim one.

avoid.name: Ecarke Finish Nailer 16 Gauge Compatible with Dewalt 20V Battery, Cordless Straight Brad Nailer
avoid.flag: Rated 2.3; heavier than the DEWALT it imitates
avoid.verdict: A DEWALT-battery clone that costs more than CRAFTSMAN's CMCN616B and rates far worse. If you're on DEWALT batteries, save for the DCN662B or DCN660B.
reasons: It's rated 2.2 stars, far below every nailer we rank (4.2 and up).
At 8.95 lbs it's nearly 3 lbs heavier than the DEWALT DCN662B it's built to run alongside, and its title calls it both a finish nailer and a 'brad nailer'.
It's a third-party body on DEWALT batteries, so DEWALT doesn't warrant it, and the listing names no warranty of its own.

buyers_guide.a: Cordless nailers skip the compressor and hose, which saves setup time on small jobs and punch lists. They're heavier (6 to 9 lbs vs 4 lbs) and cost more. For all-day production trim, an air nailer is lighter and cheaper.
Angled magazines reach into corners and under cabinets more easily, and most 15-gauge nailers are angled. Straight 16-gauge nails cost less.

buyers_guide.q: Do cordless nailers have a delay?
buyers_guide.a: Some flywheel designs spin up for a moment before firing. Air-spring designs like Metabo HPT's fire immediately, closer to a pneumatic nailer.
Makers quote 375 to 800 nails per charge on a 2.0Ah battery, depending on the tool and the wood. A spare battery covers a full day of trim.

buyers_guide.q: Can a finish nailer do framing?
buyers_guide.a: No. Finish nailers drive 15 or 16-gauge nails for trim. Framing, sheathing and subfloor need a framing nailer with 2- to 3-1/2-inch clipped or round-head nails.
